habitat: Pairs and small parties in tree canopies in forest at all altitudes, and in adjacent forested kloofs and plantation fringes.
summary: A common endemic resident. Heavily streaked yellow, boldest in northern birds, with a small dark mask. The immature resembles the adult. The usual call is a thin tweetoo, twee-ee, and it also has a brisk sibilant warbling song. Newman’s size field is blank, so no length was stored. The stub has no Kemp estimate and none was added.

similar.note: Streaky-headed Seedeater is white below with a streaked crown and no breast streaks. Forest Canary is heavily streaked yellow and has a small dark mask.
Newman says the Forest Canary call is similar to the co-occurring Swee Waxbill. The canary is a streaked yellow bird. Swee Waxbill has a yellow belly and a red rump.

population.notes: No sourced Kruger estimate is currently available; taxonomy or later records require separate research.

head.pattern: Small dark mask. Heavily streaked yellow appearance, boldest in northern birds.

viewNotes.note: Heavily streaked yellow, with a small dark mask.
The streaking and the small dark mask are the front marks.
A separate flight pattern was not described. It keeps to tree canopies.

calls.description: A thin, plaintive tweetoo, twee-ee, given frequently, plus a brisk sibilant warbling song. Grade A song from Haenertsburg. The filename is a timestamp and says the file was run through an online audio converter.
